tasks.short: Maintain passenger-space inventory and provide current availability.

steps.what: Inspect reservations, holds and available space in the reservation system.
Compare partner allotments against the reservation inventory.
Agree corrections for disputed counts, holds or allotments.
Enter authorised blocks, releases and corrections in the reservation system.
Tell passengers or colleagues how much space remains.

tasks.design: Configure a live availability view in the reservation system {OTHER}; a connector compares permitted allotment data from the {PARTNER_PORTAL} and queues discrepancies in the {WORKFLOW}. Validated allocation requests and approved corrections update the {OTHER} with capacity checks, duplicate protection and an audit trail. Structured availability answers use the same inventory version and show when it was last confirmed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Booking transactions already update inventory automatically, but partner allotments and exceptional corrections often cross separate interfaces.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing inventory controls can be configured, while AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building adapters and reconciliation checks.
tasks.still_hard: Concurrent sales, expired holds, delayed partner updates and disputed capacity require reliable transaction controls and operational decisions.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve competing claims on scarce capacity and recognise when a technically valid allocation would cause an operational problem.

ambition.what: Review expiring group holds before each release deadline.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from checking counts and rekeying changes to resolving allocation conflicts. Within delegated limits, the agent can release expired holds without waiting for a weekly reconciliation.

reach.task: Review capacity exceptions and release priorities.
reach.learn: Understand allotment contracts, hold deadlines and delegated capacity limits.

evidence.claim: Capacity checks, hold expiry and structured inventory reconciliation can use deterministic rules.
Order imports and stock synchronisation demonstrate an adjacent integration pattern, not passenger-inventory capability.

assumptions: The setting includes partner allotments and occasional manual inventory corrections.
Ordinary booking transactions already update inventory; the proposal addresses remaining clerk work.
Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured savings.
The structured-input prior supports rules and integration; a language model adds little here.
Access effort excludes any extended consultation process required by national rules.
unknowns: Which reservation interfaces support versioned reads, conditional writes and hold expiry?
Which source is authoritative when partner and internal counts differ?
What allocation decisions may the agent make without controller approval?
What access approvals and consultation under national rules apply?
research_questions: Can existing reservation configuration remove the need for a custom reconciliation connector?
How does the interface prevent duplicate updates and overselling during concurrent transactions?
new_work: Investigate stale feeds and unmatched allotments.
Maintain identifier mappings, hold rules and delegated limits.
Monitor failed writes and reconcile after outages.

tasks.short: Announce confirmed arrivals, departures and movement changes through public-address equipment.

steps.what: Read arrival, departure and location updates in the transport operations system.
Confirm changed or unclear movement details with operations staff.
Prepare announcement wording using the approved phrase sheet.
Broadcast arrival and departure information through the public-address console.

tasks.design: Feed confirmed movement data from the transport operations system {OTHER} into approved templates and recorded phrases in the public-address system {OTHER}. A preview shows the service, destination, location and broadcast zone for the reservation agent to approve before release. Unclear updates return to operations staff for confirmation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Movement data and public-address controls may be separate, while staff rely on local phrase sheets and microphone routines.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing announcement features can provide templates, recorded phrases and release controls; a small deterministic connector supplies movement facts.
tasks.still_hard: Last-minute changes, conflicting instructions, pronunciation, audibility and correct zone selection need operational testing.
tasks.human_edge: Notice passenger confusion, interpret urgent instructions and choose when a live clarification is necessary.
tasks.altitude: The agent spends less time composing and speaking routine announcements and more time helping passengers interpret changes. No new operational decision rights are assumed.

reach.learn: Learn escalation protocols, zone priorities and accessible passenger communication.

evidence.claim: Approved phrases populated from structured movement data can automate routine announcement preparation without a language model.
Public-address integration and intelligibility require local validation; the digest provides no direct deployment case.

assumptions: The site has a controlled public-address console and approved routine wording.
The estimates cover routine movement announcements; emergency command remains a separate procedure.
Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates.
The human-work prior fits situational confirmation, but routine wording and playback can use existing configuration.
Consultation under national rules, where required, may extend the access phase.
unknowns: Can the public-address equipment accept structured messages and enforce zone permissions?
Which movement updates require operations confirmation?
Who may authorise routine broadcasts and urgent overrides?
Which language, accessibility and national consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Can existing announcement configuration provide previews, cancellation and duplicate suppression?
How should stale or contradictory movement updates block playback?
new_work: Maintain approved phrases and pronunciation recordings.
Test zone routing and audibility after equipment changes.
Review failed, delayed or duplicate announcements.
Keep movement-source mappings and escalation contacts current.

tasks.short: Issue authorised tickets and insurance documents, assemble itineraries and deliver the travel pack.

steps.what: Retrieve the booking, passenger details and purchased services from the reservation system.
Check names, itinerary, payment status and recorded traveller authorisation against issuance requirements.
Issue transport tickets in the ticketing system after resolving validation exceptions.
Request the traveller's selected insurance policy through the supplier portal.
Assemble tickets, policies, itinerary and joining instructions into a travel pack.
Send the travel pack to the confirmed recipient.

tasks.design: Use the reservation and ticketing system {OTHER} to validate structured booking data and prepare issuance actions, with separate approval before ticket or policy commitments take effect. A deterministic generator assembles issued documents from the {OTHER} and {PARTNER_PORTAL} into a versioned travel pack in the {DOCS}, then the {EMAIL} sends a secure link to the confirmed recipient. Role-based access and retention settings support GDPR requirements.
tasks.previous_blocker: Booking data, supplier issuance and document assembly sit across separate interfaces, with manual checks preventing costly mistakes.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing issuance features, reusable templates and smaller integration components can remove copying without changing supplier authority.
tasks.still_hard: Name mismatches, unusual fares, supplier outages, insurance permissions and irreversible issuance require careful exception handling.
tasks.human_edge: Explain restrictive terms, resolve conflicting traveller details and verify informed instructions before financial commitments.

ambition.what: Versioned travel packs refreshed after confirmed itinerary changes.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling attachments to resolving booking and policy exceptions. The agent can correct presentation errors within delegated limits; commercial commitments still require the relevant issuance approval.

reach.task: Handle document corrections after a confirmed itinerary change.
reach.learn: Learn document versioning, fare restrictions and the boundary between correction and reissue.

evidence.claim: Structured booking data and fixed templates can generate itineraries and assemble issued documents deterministically.
Existing ticketing and supplier interfaces can support issuance, subject to contractual permissions and local capabilities.

assumptions: The traveller has already chosen the services and explicitly authorised purchase.
Insurance work means requesting an authorised supplier policy, not generating policy terms or selecting cover.
Standard bookings have structured issuance rules; unfamiliar terms enter a human exception queue.
Document-heavy work mainly concerns outputs, so the document-input prior does not justify a model loop.
Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates.
Consultation under national rules, where applicable, is included in access planning.
unknowns: Which issuance actions can existing configuration support?
What supplier permissions and insurance distribution responsibilities apply?
Where are traveller authorisation and confirmed recipient details recorded?
Which GDPR retention periods, access controls and national consultation duties apply?
How often do unusual terms require manual interpretation?
research_questions: Can issuance retries safely detect an existing ticket or policy before submitting again?
Can one booking version bind validation, issuance and document assembly?
Which supplier documents must be preserved unchanged in the travel pack?
new_work: Resolve validation failures and unusual fare or policy conditions.
Check uncertain issuance outcomes before retrying.
Maintain templates, supplier mappings and issuance rules.
Handle failed delivery and revoke superseded document links.

tasks.short: Obtain current supplier brochures and maintain a usable travel-information library.

steps.what: Review the literature library for missing, outdated or depleted supplier material.
Email routine requests for replacement brochures to supplier contacts.
Call suppliers to chase missing material or arrange printed copies.
Check received literature for currency, relevant destinations and permitted use.

loop.input: New supplier literature, source address and required metadata fields.
loop.output: Dates, destinations, languages and usage statements with page references and supporting quotations.
loop.check: Validate the schema and quoted text; flag missing dates and ambiguous usage statements for human review.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per document; unreadable or oversized material goes to manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier documents vary in layout and wording; fixed fields and date matching cannot reliably locate every relevant statement.

steps.what: File approved material and tell colleagues where to find it.

tasks.design: Replace routine brochure requests with a catalogue of approved supplier links and permitted feeds in the {DOCS}; scheduled checks on the {DATA_PLATFORM} identify changed sources and missing material. A bounded extraction loop prepares cited metadata, while the reservation agent approves inclusion in the library through the {WORKFLOW}. Suppliers without usable digital sources enter a targeted contact queue.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier material arrives in inconsistent formats, dates are often unclear and printed-copy requests depend on personal contacts.
tasks.enabler_now: A link catalogue removes much routine chasing; inexpensive change checks and bounded document extraction make maintenance practical.
tasks.still_hard: A live link does not prove current content, usage rights may be ambiguous and some passengers or suppliers still need print.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether material is useful and trustworthy for passengers, and maintain supplier relationships when information is missing.

ambition.what: A curated plain-language literature collection for travellers with low literacy.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from blanket requests to curating useful material and resolving source gaps. The agent gains delegated authority to retire stale items and prioritise accessible replacements.

reach.task: Maintain approved supplier-information templates and source records.
reach.learn: Learn provenance tracking, document metadata and plain-language selection criteria.

evidence.claim: Approved source catalogues and scheduled link checks can replace routine requests where current digital material is available.
Bounded extraction can prepare document metadata, but currency, suitability and usage ambiguity still require review.

assumptions: Most routine replacement requests concern material available through approved links or permitted subscriptions.
The eliminated request step is replaced by source access; offline suppliers remain in the contact queue.
Phone and print work is concentrated in exceptions, despite the prior's high in-person share.
A working link alone never establishes publication currency or permission to redistribute.
Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates.
Access planning includes any applicable consultation under national rules.
unknowns: Which suppliers provide current links, feeds or subscriptions?
How much demand remains for printed literature?
Which material may be stored, redistributed or adapted?
Who may approve and retire library items?
Which access approvals and national consultation duties apply?
research_questions: Which source checks distinguish meaningful updates from cosmetic page changes?
How accurately can extraction locate validity dates and usage statements in representative literature?
What criteria would make the plain-language collection useful to its intended travellers?
new_work: Review changed documents and ambiguous validity dates.
Contact suppliers with unavailable or unsuitable digital material.
Maintain approved source addresses and extraction checks.
Retire stale versions and verify redistribution permissions.
Review the plain-language collection with intended users.

role.altitude: The role shifts toward resolving capacity, issuance and passenger-information exceptions. Proposed decision rights cover bounded hold releases, document presentation corrections and literature curation; operational and purchase approvals stay attached to their specific actions.
reach: First-line supervisor: coordinate capacity exceptions and disruption communication.
Customer service representative: resolve document corrections after itinerary changes.
Correspondence clerk: maintain approved supplier information and source records.
skills_to_grow: Reservation inventory controls and concurrent-update risks.
Exception triage and integration failure diagnosis.
role.ambitious_version: A journey-information coordinator who anticipates expiring holds, keeps confirmed travel documents current and curates accessible passenger guidance.

job.title: Reservation and Transportation Ticket Agents and Travel Clerks
